summary: 12 source-anchored research claims on LiteLLM Anthropic Messages interoperability, grouped by facet. Original confidence and source-owner limits are retained.

facts.text: LiteLLM exposes /v1/messages and an Anthropic-format SDK entry point for non-Anthropic providers; endpoint availability does not imply lossless Anthropic feature parity.
facts.note: confidence low; single-owner LiteLLM evidence; qualify exact deployment · confidence: low

facts.text: The Chat bridge maps client-tool input_schema into OpenAI function parameters; the schema describes arguments, while tool execution stays with the client application.
facts.note: confidence medium; native contracts do not independently certify LiteLLM implementation · confidence: medium

facts.text: The Chat bridge maps assistant tool_use blocks to function tool_calls and user tool_result blocks to role=tool messages, preserving call/result correlation through id and tool_call_id.
facts.note: confidence medium; native contracts do not independently certify LiteLLM implementation · confidence: medium

facts.text: On the Chat return path, LiteLLM reconstructs tool_use blocks from structured tool_calls and maps finish_reason=tool_calls to stop_reason=tool_use.
facts.note: confidence medium; native contracts do not independently certify LiteLLM implementation · confidence: medium

facts.text: For client function tools, the application executes each selected call and returns its result; generating a tool block does not perform the operation.
facts.note: confidence high; native contracts do not independently certify LiteLLM implementation · confidence: high

facts.text: The Chat adapter maps Anthropic tool_choice any to required, auto to auto, tool to a named function, and none to none; downstream support remains a separate check.
facts.note: confidence low; single-owner LiteLLM evidence; qualify exact deployment · confidence: low

facts.text: At the inspected commit, openai/ Messages requests use Responses by default. For a chat-only target, use_chat_completions_url_for_anthropic_messages selects the Chat bridge instead.
facts.note: confidence low; single-owner LiteLLM evidence; qualify exact deployment · confidence: low

facts.text: If the upstream implements Messages natively, model_info.supported_endpoints can opt into /v1/messages passthrough; ordinary OpenAI compatibility alone is insufficient for that opt-in.
facts.note: confidence low; single-owner LiteLLM evidence; qualify exact deployment · confidence: low

facts.text: LiteLLM's Chat-stream wrapper emits Anthropic block lifecycle events and input_json_delta fragments. Clients must assemble tool arguments by block and wait for closure before parsing them.
facts.note: confidence medium; native contracts do not independently certify LiteLLM implementation · confidence: medium

facts.text: Verify native function-tool capability and model-specific parsing before using a translated local backend for agent work; an API wrapper cannot supply missing model competence.
facts.note: confidence medium; native contracts do not independently certify LiteLLM implementation · confidence: medium

facts.text: Treat initial HTTP 200 as provisional for streamed generation: Anthropic errors can arrive in SSE after headers, and LiteLLM's Messages router explicitly handles stream error events.
facts.note: confidence medium; native contracts do not independently certify LiteLLM implementation · confidence: medium

facts.text: Translation can approximate or lose Anthropic-only details. Native passthrough also reduces cache_control to its portable core unless cache_control_ttl is enabled; avoid promising byte-for-byte fidelity.
facts.note: confidence low; single-owner LiteLLM evidence; qualify exact deployment · confidence: low

evidenceQualification.scope: Documentation and pinned-code research; native provider sources do not certify the gateway implementation.
